recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. The current source reflects the applied FHIR-47629 resolution as refined by the later applied FHIR-48379 decision; changing the source now would either duplicate existing guidance or undo later approved wording.
issue_request: FHIR-47629 was Applied with a Not Persuasive with Modification resolution asking FHIR-core to clarify that normative upper cardinality changes from 1 to * can break older JSON parsers, to minimize such changes where possible by adding sibling elements, and to add a JSON repeating-elements warning that processors should handle repeatability changes across versions.
initial_application: Git commit 0a5592638b4ebfaa8352e8ec5f9b2ae0044e7a71, "Changes from FHIR-47629.", edited source/versions.html and source/json.html to add the cardinality anchor, JSON compatibility caution, minimized-cardinality-change sentence, and JSON dragon warning. The combined branch already contains those source changes, but did not previously contain an Issue-Reconcile-Key audit commit for FHIR-47629.
additional_context: FHIR-I WGM minutes from September 2024 record the 16-0-8 vote, the JSON breakage concern, the new-sibling guidance, and an explicit decision to raise a FHIRPath follow-up. That follow-up is FHIR-48379, an Applied issue that changed the same paragraph from "JSON issue" to "JSON and FHIRPath issues" and added FHIRPath warning language. FHIR-48379 already has its own reconciliation commit on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source/versions.html cardinality row warns about JSON path changes and FHIRPath expressions, and says normative cardinality changes will be minimized, for example by defining new sibling elements. The current source/json.html repeating-elements section contains the requested dragon warning that repeatability may change between versions and processors should be prepared.

related_jiras.note: Applied follow-up that extended the same cardinality warning from JSON-only to JSON and FHIRPath and already has a separate reconciliation commit on the combined branch.
